description.narrative: TradeMark Africa's Regional Private Sector Development Programme works to embed private sector voice and leadership at the heart of Africa's trade agenda, recognising that sustainable and inclusive trade growth requires businesses, not just governments and institutions, to actively shape the policy environment, drive standards compliance, and unlock export opportunities across the continent. The Programme operates through a structured Private Sector Engagement Framework that provides a systematic approach to deepening collaboration between TMA, business associations, and enterprises at national and regional levels, with a particular focus on two complementary roles: enabling the private sector to identify, report, and advocate for the removal of non-tariff barriers and trade policy constraints in support of the Trade and Investment Environment Portfolio; and building enterprise capacity to meet international standards, access certification, and compete in regional and global value chains in support of the Quality and Value of Traded Goods Portfolio. Cutting across both, the Programme champions inclusive economic participation by implementing TMA's Gender and Inclusion Strategy to ensure that women-led enterprises, youth entrepreneurs, and underserved businesses are not only beneficiaries of trade reform but active participants in shaping it, in alignment with AfCFTA's continental market vision.

recipient-country.narrative: TradeMark Africa (TMA) accelerates economic integration across 20 sub-Saharan nations by designing regional programmes that reduce trade barriers, lower transit costs, and digitize border infrastructure. Spanning East, West, Central, Southern Africa, and the Horn, these initiatives modernise critical maritime ports and key trade corridors by replacing paper-heavy customs processes with automated digital single-window systems. By targeting green trade corridor development, supporting women and small businesses in cross-border trade, and mobilizing private capital through its commercial arm, Trade Catalyst Africa, TMA directly facilitates trade flow alignment with the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) frameworks.

provider-org.narrative: Denmark - Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Danida

receiver-org.narrative: TradeMark Africa (TMA) is a leading Aid-for-Trade organisation founded in 2010 to grow intra-African trade, increase Africa’s share in global trade, and make trade more pro-poor and sustainable. We operate on a not-for-profit basis, funded by a strong coalition of development partners including Canada, Denmark, the European Union, Finland, France, the Gates Foundation, Ireland, the Mastercard Foundation, the Netherlands, Norway, Sweden and the United Kingdom. TMA works closely with regional and continental institutions, national governments, the private sector, and civil society to unlock trade and investment opportunities across the continent.

title.narrative: Increased Market Access and Business Competitiveness
Number of jobs created, sustained and improved as a result of TMA projects

comment.narrative: About 1,200 jobs sustained in Kenya and Tanzania under the EAGC project

title.narrative: Value of goods exported supported by TMA interventions

description.narrative: Value in USD(m)

comment.narrative: $4.8 million sales of 7,500 tonnes of grains generated (EAGC- $ 4.3 million & AUXFIN -$0.5 million) with about 140 tonnes of soymeal traded through the Moyale border under the EAGC project. Approximately 5,500 smallholder producers and enterprises, farmers, aggregators, and traders, have participated in capacity building initiatives and agribusiness expos in Kenya and Tanzania to improve productivity, access technologies, and strengthen market linkages. Of these 56% are women and women-owned enterprises and 30% youth.

title.narrative: Volume of exports supported by TMA interventions

description.narrative: Volume in Metric Tonnes

comment.narrative: $4.8 million sales of 7,500 tonnes of grains generated (EAGC- $ 4.3 million & AUXFIN -$0.5 million) with about 140 tonnes of soymeal traded through the Moyale border under the EAGC project. Approximately 5,500 smallholder producers and enterprises, farmers, aggregators, and traders, have participated in capacity building initiatives and agribusiness expos in Kenya and Tanzania to improve productivity, access technologies, and strengthen market linkages. Of these 56% are women and women-owned enterprises and 30% youth.
